parts.label: (a)(i)
hints: Hint 1: Forget physical hardness like a hard solid. Think about what happens when the beam meets tissue - does it get absorbed easily or pass right through to the detector?
parts.proper_answer: Hardness is a measure of the penetrating power of the X-ray beam.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **What Hard Really Means Here**
Think of a soft beam as one that is easily stopped and a hard beam as one that is tough to stop. In the body, soft low-energy X-rays are absorbed by soft tissue, while hard high-energy X-rays pass through much more material.

Step 2: **Clean Definition**
So hardness tells you how penetrating the beam is. A harder beam has higher photon energy and greater penetration.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
key_concepts: electron energy and X-ray photon energy
hints: Hint 1: Focus on what gives the electrons their energy just before they hit the metal target. Which p.d. between cathode and anode controls how much kinetic energy they gain?
parts.proper_answer: Decrease the accelerating voltage (p.d. between cathode and anode).
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Linking Voltage to Hardness**
Electrons are boiled off the heated cathode and then accelerated toward the anode. The kinetic energy they gain comes from the accelerating p.d., $eV$. When they hit the target this energy sets the energy of the X-ray photons produced.

Step 2: **Making the Beam Softer**
To make the beam less penetrating you need lower-energy photons, so you give the electrons less energy to start with. That means you lower the accelerating voltage between cathode and anode.

parts.label: (b)
hints: Hint 1: Compare the pictures. A plain X-ray is a single 2D shadow where structures overlap. Think about what many X-ray slices taken from all around the body and built up by computer can show.
Hint 2: Think about the price paid for that extra detail in terms of radiation exposure, time, staying still, and cost.
parts.proper_answer: Advantage: CT gives a 3D image showing depth / internal structure can be viewed from any angle without overlap. Disadvantage: greater X-ray exposure with increased health risk / more expensive / patient must remain stationary for longer.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Why CT Shows More**
A standard X-ray is one flat projection, so bone, soft tissue and organs all overlap in one shadow. A CT scanner rotates around you, takes many thin slices and a computer reconstructs them into a 3D volume. That gives depth information and clear slices through soft tissue that a plain film hides.

Step 2: **Why CT Costs More**
All those extra views mean many more exposures, so the total radiation dose is much larger than for a single X-ray, increasing risk. The scan also takes longer, is more expensive, and any movement blurs the reconstruction, so you must lie very still.
